evidence: src/application/catalogue-service.ts: `public addProduct(input: CreateProductDto, request?: Request): ProductDto` puts the Express HTTP Request type in the signature of the application use case, which is a transport/framework concern that belongs to infrastructure.
The `request` parameter is never used in the body of addProduct, so it only couples the use case to the HTTP framework.

The rest of the file fits the application role: it orchestrates the repository through `this.products.findById` and `this.products.save`, constructs the domain object with `new Product(...)`, and maps to DTOs with `toDto`.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: CatalogueService is an application-layer use-case service. Most of what it does fits that role: it coordinates the ProductRepository port, checks for a duplicate id through the repository, builds the Product domain object, saves it and maps it to DTOs. The problem is the public use-case method `addProduct(input: CreateProductDto, request?: Request)`. Its signature accepts an Express HTTP `Request`, which makes transport and framework concerns part of the application contract. That responsibility belongs to the infrastructure/presentation adapter, the controller. The use case should only receive the DTO. The parameter is unused, which shows it does nothing here except couple the use case to the HTTP transport. I treated the `import { Request } from "express"` statement as out of scope because it is about import direction. The failure is that a transport type is part of the method contract. That is why confidence is moderate.

violations.message: CatalogueService.addProduct accepts `request?: Request` (Express). The HTTP/framework request type belongs to the infrastructure/presentation layer, not the application use-case contract. The controller should map the request to CreateProductDto and the service should take only the DTO.
